The effect appeared to be brand specific6-8 and as- sociated particularly with the subcutaneous use of preparations containing polysorbate 80 as a stabiliser.9 Other possible causes have been proposed including contamination with silicone lubri- cant used in pre-filled syringes or release of organic compounds from rubber plungers.10 Subsequently, manufacturers have re- ported that cases of red cell aplasia with neutralising antibodies have also occurred in chronic renal failure patients treated with subcutaneous darbepoetin alfa.11 They also warn that because of cross-reactivity, patients who develop antibody-mediated anae- mia with either an epoetin or darbepoetin alfa should not be swapped to another erythropoietic protein. Epoetin-induced red cell aplasia has been managed with with- drawal of the epoetin and treatment with immunosuppressants including corticosteroids, cyclophosphamide, and ciclosporin. Intravenous normal immunoglobulin has also been used. Kidney transplantation is reported to bring about a rapid recovery.10,12 1. Smith KJ, et al. The cardiovascular effects of erythropoietin.
